To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a C-terminal domain of Xenopus cdc25B is required for induction but not for activation of cdc2 kinase in vivo.
a C-terminal region of cdc 25B is required for induction, but not maintenance, of oocyte maturation.

a C-terminal domain in cdc25B is required for induction and that a region in cdc25A that is similar in sequence is required for dominant-negative inhibition of cdc25-dependent germinal vesicle break down.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the cdc25 region responsible for induction of GVDB.
the identification of the C-terminal cdc2-cdc25 interaction domain of cdc25.
identifying regions of cdc25 protein that are involved in regulation of the cell cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C-terminal 200 amino acids of cdc25 are required for GVBD, and that the region between amino acids 356 and 556 is required for the dominant negative inhibition of GVBD.
the C-termini of cdc25A and cdc25B are involved in both activation of the cell cycle and in the inhibition of cdc25-dependent activation of the cell division cycle.
cdc25B is a protein phosphatase that promotes entry of cells into mitosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-terminus of Cdc25B is required for its activation, while the C-terminis is required to inhibit the activation of the enzyme.
cdc25B contains two regions of peptide sequence, one at the N-terminus and the other at the C- terminus, both of which are involved in promoting GVBD.
a C-terminal domain of cdc25 is involved in both positive and negative regulation of the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-termini of cdc25 proteins play important roles in the regulation of cell-cycle progression.
the cdc25B protein is able to induce germinal vesicle break down (a hallmark of oocyte maturation) in Xenopus oocytes when microinjected.
the C-terminal domain of Cdc25 is important for its ability to promote GVBD.
